Dianna Russini is looking back at her transition back to sports media. The former Athletic NFL insider and reporter has begun her new show on BetUS, The Russini Report, which aired its first episode on Wednesday, Nov. 11. The premiere marked her return to sports media following the fallout from her photo scandal with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. “Feeling loved. Feeling grateful. Back talking football, and I couldn’t do it without the best friends and family in the world. More to come…” she wrote in the caption on her Nov. 19 Instagram post. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Several fans came into the comment section to support her next step. “You know your people… it’s allllllll noise,” one fan wrote. “LETS GO GIRL. The mic is yours.” “Welcome back!!!!!! And all the love,” another fan wrote. View this post on Instagram Seven months ago, Russini and Vrabel — who are married to other people — were seen getting cozy at a resort in Arizona via photos that were published by Page Six. While she didn’t address the scandal directly, she did talk about her personal life at the beginning of her show. “Over the last few months, I have had a lot of time to think about my life and my priorities and the person that I want to be moving forward, and being home in New Jersey with my husband and our two little boys and being truly present, it gave me so much perspective that I didn’t even know I needed,” Russini said. She then hinted at the support she received in the past few months, most likely in connection to the scandal. “It gave me so much perspective that I didn’t even know I needed. I’ve also had a lot of long conversations with people all around football. You know, some were about the game, and others were just about life to the people who picked up the phone and checked in and offered both encouragement and honest advice, from the bottom of my heart, thank you,” she added. New episodes of The Russini Report will stream live on the BetUS TV website and the official The Russini Report X account. item.title: Timberwolves HC Chris Finch hit with a tech after throwing shade at ref in Knicks game
item.description: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images Timberwolves HC Chris Finch hit with a tech after throwing shade at ref in Knicks game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Minnesota Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch let his frustration boil over in the first half of Thursday night’s game against the New York Knicks , and it earned him a technical foul. With 27.8 seconds left in the opening quarter and the Knicks holding a 31-26 lead at Target Center, Finch went after one of the referees with a pointed jab , telling the official, “No one came to watch you.” Finch was assessed a technical foul for the remark. "No one came to watch you." Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Chris Finch to the refs during Timberwolves vs. Knicks 👀 Finch was assessed a technical foul. pic.twitter.com/2u1LbH9TQj — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 20, 2026 It isn’t the first time Finch has run into trouble with officials. Last season, the veteran coach was hit with two technical fouls and ejected with 6:19 left in the first quarter of a Dec. 19 game against the Oklahoma City Thunder. The NBA later fined him $35,000 for directing improper language toward the officials and being slow to leave the court. Finch was also tossed from a Jan. 29, 2025, game against the Phoenix Suns , the first ejection of his career, after making derogatory comments toward the officiating crew. The technical didn’t spark a turnaround for Minnesota, either. The Knicks continued to pull away in the second quarter and took a 65-50 lead into halftime, at one point going up by as many as 18 points. New York was red-hot from the field in the first half, shooting 57.1% overall and knocking down 10 of its 16 attempts from beyond the arc. Former Timberwolves star Karl-Anthony Towns did plenty of damage against his old team, scoring 17 points and grabbing eight rebounds before the break. OG Anunoby chipped in 13 points on 5-of-7 shooting. Jaden McDaniels did his best to keep the Timberwolves within striking distance, scoring 11 points on a perfect 4-of-4 shooting, including three triples. LaMelo Ball added nine points on 4-of-11 shooting , while Jonathan Kuminga had seven. As a team, Minnesota shot 43.9% from the field. Minnesota entered Thursday’s contest with an 11-4 record, having won two straight games against the Portland Trail Blazers earlier in the week. item.title: Louisville takes care of Stetson, 83-69
item.description: Nov 19, 2026; Louisville, Kentucky, USA; Louisville Cardinals guard Jackson Shelstad (3) dribbles against Stetson Hatters guard Daniel MacGregor (4) during the first half at KFC Yum! Center. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Rhodes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Louisville started slow and finished slow, but put together a solid enough effort in between to come away with an 83-69 win over Stetson Thursday night inside the KFC Yum Center. The Cardinals, a 36.5-point favorite, fell behind by eight points in the first half and led by just five at the break. Flory Bidunga proved to be the ultimate difference maker against a Stetson team that entered the evening 0-4 against Division-I competition. The Kansas transfer dominated on both ends of the floor, finishing with 25 points, 12 rebounds, four blocks and three assists. An injury to point guard Seth Trimble allowed Karter Knox to make his first start as a Cardinal, and the Arkansas transfer responded in a major way. Knox scored 14 points and also snatched 10 rebounds. Adrian Wooley became the third Cardinal to record a double-double, scoring 19 points and grabbing 10 boards. Louisville won handily despite once again struggling from beyond the arc, where it shot just 7-of-28 (25.0 percent). They more than made up for it with their pressure at the rim, an effort spearheaded by Bidunga, who drew nine fouls and got to the free-throw line eight times. This was not the start to finish ass kicking that I think we all were hoping to see in the wake of the Memphis embarrassment. For whatever reason, it still seems like these guys can’t get it through their heads that they simply are not good enough to manhandle anyone when they’re out there just sort of going through the motions. They should have ample evidence now. For a multitude of reasons, next week’s three (or, ideally, four) games in Vegas could not be more important. The show starts Tuesday night against maybe the best team in the entire field in Texas Tech. Here’s hoping we’re ready.

item.title: Buccaneers at Lions: Thursday injury report for Week 11
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers warms up before the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received some encouraging news Thursday as they continued preparations for their Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions. After missing Wednesday’s practice, quarterback Baker Mayfield (foot/right thumb) returned to the practice field Thursday as a limited participant. It’s a positive development for the veteran quarterback, whose availability for Sunday has been in question since suffering a foot injury against the Chicago Bears. Mayfield revealed Thursday that the injury occurred early in the game against Chicago during a scramble that resulted in a completion to running back Kenny Gainwell. He played through the discomfort for the remainder of the contest. When asked about his readiness to play against Detroit, Mayfield responded, “I feel ready.” While his return to practice is certainly encouraging, the Buccaneers are expected to make a determination on his availability Friday. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels remains the next man up should Mayfield be unable to play. Unfortunately for Tampa Bay, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) missed his second consecutive practice, while outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) remained limited. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. and running back Bucky Irving were added to Thursday’s injury report as non-participants, while defensive lineman A’Shawn Robinson was limited. All three received rest designations. Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) remained full participants. For Detroit, there were no changes to its injury report from Wednesday. Center Cade Mays (ankle) remained sidelined, while six players, including cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder), remained limited. Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) was once again a full participant. Both teams will release their final injury reports Friday, with much of the attention in Tampa Bay continuing to surround Mayfield and whether he will be healthy enough to lead the Buccaneers’ offense Sunday in Detroit.

item.title: Phil Gould Takes Over Stewart Friesen’s Truck For 2027
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images In the 2027 NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series, Stewart Friesen and his No. 52 Toyota Tundra TRD Pro team will have Phil Gould serving as crew chief. This pairing was confirmed on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, by Speedway Media . Gould steps away from his role as competition director at Niece Motorsports to take the lead on the Halmar Friesen Racing entry. The change targets a specific goal: turning a solid driver into a consistent winner. A Resume Built on Wins He has already notched eight victories across his career in the Truck division. His record includes 44 top-five finishes and 87 top-10 results over an eight-year span. He worked with 14 different drivers, including stars like Ross Chastain and Carson Hocevar. In 2023 alone, he guided Hocevar to four wins. He also secured a victory with Chastain at Darlington Raceway in May 2024. That experience is rare and valuable for a team looking to climb the standings. The move comes after a season where Friesen himself finished 12th in the driver’s standings. Friesen managed four top-five results and nine top-10 results while working with crew chief Dustin Dunn. He led 31 laps and held an average finishing spot of 17.7. Still, the effort was enough to hit a major milestone. By finishing fifth at the Homestead-Miami Speedway finale, Friesen earned his 100th career top-10 in the Truck division. That stat proves the driver has the speed, but the team needs the right mind to lock it down. The Shift at Halmar Friesen Halmar Friesen Racing is making a clear statement with this hire. The organization wants to move past just being competitive and start winning races. Friesen has been in the Truck division for 11 seasons. He knows the series better than most, but he needs a partner who has been there before. Gould first took on crew chief responsibilities in 2013 within the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series. He spent two seasons with Brian Scott at Richard Childress Racing before moving to Roush Fenway Racing in 2015. His work with Ryan Reed led to a first-ever victory at Daytona in 2017. That win proved he can handle the pressure of big stages. Gould also helped Niece Motorsports reach the Playoffs with Chastain in his first Truck season as a crew chief. The duo finished as runners-up in the final standings. They notched three victories that year. This history shows Gould can build a championship-level operation from the ground up. He knows how to manage different drivers and extract the best performance from them. The team is betting that his past success will translate to the No. 52 truck. Looking Toward the 2027 Season The 2027 season will be the first time this new combination hits the track together. item.content:encoded: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images In the 2027 NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series, Stewart Friesen and his No. 52 Toyota Tundra TRD Pro team will have Phil Gould serving as crew chief. This pairing was confirmed on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, by Speedway Media . Gould steps away from his role as competition director at Niece Motorsports to take the lead on the Halmar Friesen Racing entry. The change targets a specific goal: turning a solid driver into a consistent winner. A Resume Built on Wins He has already notched eight victories across his career in the Truck division. His record includes 44 top-five finishes and 87 top-10 results over an eight-year span. He worked with 14 different drivers, including stars like Ross Chastain and Carson Hocevar. In 2023 alone, he guided Hocevar to four wins. He also secured a victory with Chastain at Darlington Raceway in May 2024. That experience is rare and valuable for a team looking to climb the standings. The move comes after a season where Friesen himself finished 12th in the driver’s standings. Friesen managed four top-five results and nine top-10 results while working with crew chief Dustin Dunn. He led 31 laps and held an average finishing spot of 17.7. Still, the effort was enough to hit a major milestone. By finishing fifth at the Homestead-Miami Speedway finale, Friesen earned his 100th career top-10 in the Truck division. That stat proves the driver has the speed, but the team needs the right mind to lock it down. The Shift at Halmar Friesen Halmar Friesen Racing is making a clear statement with this hire. The organization wants to move past just being competitive and start winning races. Friesen has been in the Truck division for 11 seasons. He knows the series better than most, but he needs a partner who has been there before. Gould first took on crew chief responsibilities in 2013 within the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series. He spent two seasons with Brian Scott at Richard Childress Racing before moving to Roush Fenway Racing in 2015. His work with Ryan Reed led to a first-ever victory at Daytona in 2017. That win proved he can handle the pressure of big stages. Gould also helped Niece Motorsports reach the Playoffs with Chastain in his first Truck season as a crew chief. The duo finished as runners-up in the final standings. They notched three victories that year. This history shows Gould can build a championship-level operation from the ground up. He knows how to manage different drivers and extract the best performance from them. The team is betting that his past success will translate to the No. 52 truck. Looking Toward the 2027 Season The 2027 season will be the first time this new combination hits the track together. Friesen has spent the last year with Dunn, and now he switches to a new voice on the radio. The shift is meant to boost the team’s results immediately. Gould’s track record with young talent and veteran drivers makes him a safe bet. He has worked with everyone from Trevor Bayne to Connor Zilisch. The No. 52 team now has a crew chief who has won at Daytona, Darlington, and other tough tracks. With Gould at the helm, the team has a clear path to improvement.

Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Lewis Masella, Site Editor The Los Angeles are looking for right-handed relief options their bullpen for 2027. Yes, they still have Edgardo Henriquez , who is a rising star. They also have closer Edwin Diaz , who will, hopefully, be healthy and effective next season. However, Evan Philips has departed on a three-year deal with the Atlanta Braves. No one knows if Blake Trienien will return to the relief corps in 2027. Seth Halverson is out for the year, as it was announced yesterday that he underwent Tommy John surgery and will be out for the entire season (whenever it starts). Dodgers announced that Seth Halvorsen had Tommy John surgery yesterday. He will miss all of 2027. — Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) November 18, 2026 The reality is, every new season brings change. The question is, how will the Dodgers fill the one of the few holes on their roster next year. Free Agent Options For Right-Handed Relief Jonathan Loaisiga One of the names the Dodgers are reportedly interested in is Jonathan Loaisiga. The right-hander spent last season with the Arizona Diamondbacks. He collected a respectable 2.42 Earned Run Average in 67 games averaging an inning per outing. The thirty-two year old veteran induces a lot of ground balls with his signature sinker. Perhaps, the most impressive things about him is his minuscule walk rate which stands at five percent. Hitters have a batting average of .242. However, right-handed hitters are hitting a measly .179 against him, while left-handers hit a pretty robust .286. Thus. Loaisiga would probably considered a right-handed relief specialist. Not surprisingly, he limits hard contact and keeps the ball in the yard. His strikeout rate is not as impressive on paper. However, he doesn’t need to rely on velocity, as long as he gets outs. The biggest challenge of the right-hander’s career is not that he wasn’t effective, it was his ability to stay healthy. Loaisiga has only one season in his career where he stayed off the Injured List. It was 2021, and he was with the New York Yankees. He posted a 2.17 ERA that year. Jason Adam Another name the Dodgers could consider is Jason Adam. He has spent the last two and a half years with the division-rival San Diego Padres. He was sidelined during both ends of last season with different injuries However, when he is healthy, he has proven to be an effective setup man whose ERA hovers around two. He has a high whiff rate as well chase rate. Adam doesn’t give up many home runs, and he is accustomed to holding late leads in big games. Something the Dodgers right-handed relief core has struggled to do the past two seasons. Spears managed to score his first point at the line after the media break and got a lay in during a 10-0 run late in the game that extended the lead to 25 points. Texas remains at the Moody Center for a Sunday matchup against Southern Indiana before heading to San Diego for the Rady Children’s Invitational over Thanksgiving. item.title: Fernando Alonso Calls Dakar Challenge ‘Another Level’
item.description: Formula One F1 - United States Grand Prix - Circuit of the Americas, Austin, Texas, U.S. - October 25, 2026 Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso during the drivers parade IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Jerome Miron Fernando Alonso says the Dakar rally is a much harder test than Formula 1 racing. He told reporters that the unknown nature of the event makes it “another level” of difficulty. For a second time, the Spanish driver will return to the Dakar rally thanks to Aston Martin’s three-car lineup. His return comes after he finished third in the 2020 event while driving for Toyota. Alonso explained the mental gap between racing on a known track and racing in the wild. In Formula 1, drivers repeat the same thing lap after lap to perfect their driving style. The Dakar rally requires constant improvising because drivers do not know what happens next. He noted that the eyes cannot blink for four or five hours during the race. The focus on not blinking caused him headaches during his first test days. The Unknown Terrain The route for the 2027 Dakar will run from Portugal to Morocco. Originally scheduled for Saudi Arabia, the event was moved because of regional instability. The event’s relocation to new conditions increases the difficulty for drivers. Alonso said “And Dakar is to the unknown; every metre is new” when discussing the challenge, according to Formula1.com . He feels the task is bigger for him because he did not grow up in that type of racing. With the Dreadnought, Aston Martin will make its debut in the event. This is a real-world competition version of a car the manufacturer designed for the new game “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.” Alonso will have Marc Coma as his co-driver for the upcoming race. Learning from History Alonso knows he faces a steep climb to win the title. Sebastian Loeb, likely the greatest rally driver in history, is his teammate. Loeb has tried to win the Dakar nine or 10 times and has not achieved the win yet. Alonso said “I think I was competitive” when he reflected on his 2020 performance. He admitted he had a good six months of preparation and thousands of kilometres of driving before that race. He does not have that same amount of time or distance in his current schedule. Despite the lack of prep, Alonso says the big challenge is what makes the event appealing. He wants to attempt to win it one day in the future.

item.title: New Michigan AD on if coaches can have sex with players: ‘It just depends’
item.description: Credit: Vasha Hunt-Imagn Images The University of Michigan has reportedly landed on Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts to assume the same role in Ann Arbor, where he will replace the outgoing Warde Manuel, who oversaw national championships in both basketball and football, but also dealt with multiple scandals over his tenure. The latest scandal under Manuel involved former football head coach Sherrone Moore, who was relieved of his duties with the program after the university determined that he had an inappropriate romantic relationship with a staffer. However, Alberts’ response to a romantic scandal of his certainly raises some eyebrows. In February 2024, former Nebraska Cornhuskers women’s basketball player Ashley Scoggin sued the Nebraska Board of Regents, the women’s basketball coach, and then-AD Trev Alberts after she was dismissed from the team due to a sexual relationship with assistant coach Chuck Love. Scoggin was initially suspended before ultimately being dismissed, and Love was suspended with pay before being asked to quietly resign, according to FOIAball.com, which also reported that Alberts paid Love $136,000 in severance. FOIAball’s David Covucci reports that Scoggin’s lawsuit accuses Alberts of violating Scoggin’s civil rights by approving of her removal from the team, refusing to order an investigation, and encouraging her to leave the university. As a result of the lawsuits, Alberts sat down for a deposition with Scoggin’s attorneys across two sessions, one in December 2025 and another In February 2026, and he provided some questionable answers under oath. Alberts was given a copy of Nebraska’s policy on consensual relationships, which states: Faculty or Staff members are prohibited from engaging in any romantic relationship with an undergraduate student.” Alberts agreed that the policy also applies to coaches and student-athletes and was then directly asked: “College coaches should never have sex with the student-athletes that they are coaching. True?” “I don’t know how to answer that,” Alberts answered. “I mean, you know, it just depends.” Alberts went on to say that COVID eligibility rules led to older players, making the situations involved more “nuanced.” “You know, we don’t get involved, nor do I try to monitor. I have no idea what’s going on with relationships,” he went on to say. He was then asked if his then-current school, Texas A&M, had a zero-tolerance policy on relationships between coaches and players (they do). “I don’t know the answer to that question,” Alberts responded. Per ESPN, Michigan hasn’t formalized its contract with its AD target. It may want to do its homework before any dotted lines are signed. item.title: Heavy rain severely limits Las Vegas GP first practice
item.description: Five of the 22 drivers did not even leave the pit lane as rain lashed the Las Vegas Strip, creating extremely slippery conditions (Sona Maleterova) The first practice session for the Las Vegas F1 Grand Prix was severely limited by torrential rain on Thursday with no driver completing a timed lap. Five of the 22 racers did not even leave the pits as rain lashed the Las Vegas Strip street circuit, creating extremely slippery conditions, with temperatures hovering around 54 degrees F (12 C). Thousands of fans packed the grandstands but the only exciting moments they witnessed were a few close calls for those drivers who did venture out to test the grip of their tires. Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto both nearly lost control of their cars in puddles. The second of three practice sessions is scheduled for later Thursday evening. The race takes place Saturday. The Las Vegas Grand Prix is the 21st of 23 rounds scheduled this season, with Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes already crowned this year's champions. nb/bfi/amz/pst

item.title: Recap: OKC Blue enjoy easy-peasy 112-86 win over Mexico City Capitanes
item.description: The OKC Blue enjoyed a 112-86 win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Thursday. The home victory improved their record to 2-5 in the 2026-27 G League regular season. In a rare good start, the Blue played connective basketball. They had a 22-21 lead after the first quarter. They added to their lead with a strong second frame of 33 points. That included a 20-7 run. OKC entered halftime with a 55-43 lead over the Capitanes. The second half was much of the same story. In a rare instance, the Blue were on the right side of a lopsided affair. They blitzed Mexico City with 34 points in the third quarter. That helped them get up by 30-plus points. At that juncture, OKC held a strong 89-59 lead. The Blue were on cruise control the rest of the way. They put up 23 points in the fourth quarter. They led by as many as 31 points. The entire active roster had the chance to log serious minutes. The Blue shot 47% from the field and went 18-of-41 (43.9%) from 3. They shot 9-of-14 on free throws. They had 32 assists on 40 baskets. Five Blue players scored double-digit points. Meanwhile, the Capitanes shot 36% from the field and went 10-of-37 (27%) from 3. They shot 9-of-16 on free throws. They had 24 assists on 32 baskets. Four Capitanes players scored double-digit points. Here are some notable individual performances from both sides: Josh Dix: 21 points on 8-of-12 shooting, 5-of-9 from 3, three rebounds, two assists Robert McCray V: 21 points on 8-of-13 shooting, 4-of-6 from 3, five assists, four rebounds Christoph Tilly: 19 points on 6-of-8 shooting, 3-of-3 on free throws, 10 rebounds, four assists, two blocks Anthony Pritchard: 12 points on 5-of-10 shooting, 2-of-4 from 3, 11 assists, three rebounds Zeke Mayo: 23 points on 8-of-21 shooting, 4-of-12 from 3, 3-of-3 on free throws, five rebounds, four assists Agapy de Melo Santos: 13 points on 5-of-7 shooting, eight rebounds The full highlights of the Blue's 26-point win to the Capitanes can be watched below: This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Recap: OKC Blue enjoy easy-peasy 112-86 win over Mexico City Capitanes

Fox, the incumbent English-language World Cup partner, has reportedly submitted a joint bid with Univision, the Spanish-language broadcaster owned by TelevisaUnivision, according to John Ourand of Puck . Additionally, NBC, the incumbent Spanish-language partner which was previously reported to be taking its decision on whether or not to bid down to the wire, has opted not to submit an offer for World Cup rights. The other two corporate owners of big-four broadcast networks — Disney and Skydance — were previously reported to have decided against bidding, leaving the Fox-Univision team-up as the only offer not from a streaming service. The joint bid effectively means Fox and Univision will try to maintain the status quo by keeping the World Cup entirely on broadcast television, with the only difference being Univision stepping in for Telemundo. The remaining companies that have reportedly submitted bids consist only of streamers: Netflix, YouTube, and Amazon. Apple was previously reported to have decided against a bid. item.title: Geno Auriemma blasts NIL payouts to player that ‘hasn’t dribbled the ball one time in college’
item.description: UConn head coach Geno Auriemma gestures in the first half of an NCAA college basketball game against Ohio State in Columbus, Ohio, Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026. After landing just one of the top-10-ranked recruits in the country, UConn women’s basketball head coach Geno Auriemma questioned the idea of “paying a kid a million dollars” right out of high school. Auriemma was addressing reporters after the early national signing period for the class of 2027 recruits wrapped up and UConn had only signed No. 9-ranked Sydney Savoury. One of the biggest changes in college sports continues to be the introduction of NIL money, which has led to student-athletes earning up to millions of dollars just to play for a certain program, which seemed to frustrate Auriemma. UConn head coach Geno Auriemma gestures in the first half of an NCAA college basketball game against Ohio State in Columbus, Ohio, Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026. AP Photo/Sue Ogrocki “We just signed the No. 9 player in the country. We don’t have cachet with guys that are getting paid a million dollars to go play some place,” he told reporters . “They’re getting the cachet. I just don’t see the value of paying a high school kid a million dollars to come out of high school that hasn’t dribbled the ball one time in college. “I don’t get the idea of paying a kid a million dollars coming out of high school. That’s more than [about] 90 percent of best players in the world in the WNBA. As long as that’s the case, we’re going to get the guys we’re gonna get, but we’re not going to get the guys we’re not supposed to get.” Continuing to address the ever-evolving landscape of college recruiting, Auriemma noted how money has become such a dominant factor in where players choose to go. And he called out players and their families who have said academics and the school being the “right fit” were factors in their decision. “I don’t have those conversations with the parents,” Auriemma said. “We have an agent that talks to their agent because the kids and the parents lie to you. ‘It’s not about the money. It’s about academics. It’s about finding the right fit. It’s about the right experience.’ No it isn’t. Just say it’s about the money, and we can all live happily ever after.” UConn has gotten off to a 3-2 record to start the season, which has included losses to Michigan and Louisville. Its wins have come against Cornell, No. 10 Iowa and No. 17 Ohio State.

item.title: Iowa State stays undefeated with win over UNI
item.description: Sienna Harvey (1) of Iowa State drives against Callie Levin (23) of the University of Northern Iowa. Harvey finished with 12 points and played a team high 37 minutes. CEDAR FALLS — Tjaša Turnšek scored 16 points and Sienna Harvey added 12 as unbeaten Iowa State pulled away in the second half for a 72-57 victory over Northern Iowa at the McLeod Center Wednesday night. The Cyclones (6-0, 0-0 Big 12) closed the second quarter on a critical 9-0 run and sustained momentum down the stretch to claim their 42nd all-time victory over the Panthers (1-4, 0-0 Missouri Valley). Northern Iowa stayed competitive early through a sharp perimeter attack, sinking 10 three-pointers on the night—marking its first double-digit performance from beyond the arc this season and highest total since making 13 against Valparaiso. Abby Tuttle tied a career high with 16 points on 6-of-9 shooting to pace UNI, while Jenna Twedt and Callie Levin added 14 points each. The opening frame was tightly contested as Twedt knocked down two early 3-pointers and freshman Anna Greene banked in her first collegiate triple to keep Northern Iowa within 18-17 at the first break. The Panthers surged ahead 31-28 late in the second quarter following a free throw and a 3-pointer from Levin. However, Iowa State responded by holding UNI scoreless over the final three minutes of the half, executing a 9-0 surge to carry a 37-31 lead into the locker room. Harvey ignited the Cyclones out of halftime with consecutive baskets, helping spark a 15-4 run that pushed Iowa State’s advantage to 15 points. Northern Iowa mounted a late third-quarter response by capitalizing on several Cyclone turnovers, running off a 10-3 burst to trim the deficit to 55-47 entering the final period. Iowa State put the game away in the fourth quarter after both teams endured an early scoring drought. Arianna Jackson broke the stalemate with a 3-pointer at the 6:45 mark, sparking a pair of 7-point runs that closed out the victory. Turnšek finished an efficient 6-of-7 from the floor to lead all scorers, while Harvey contributed four assists alongside her 12 points. Xiao Zhang, Mya Babbitt and Jackson added timely depth scoring for Iowa State. For Northern Iowa, Elise Jaeger collected a team-high five rebounds, and Greene registered three blocks in 14 minutes of action. Iowa State returns home to host the Drake Bulldogs on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 2 p.m.

Things started out well enough, and the Penguins even took a 1-0 lead, but the St. Louis Blues scored the next four goals on the way to a 5-2 win. According to ESPN Research, 77% of teams in a playoff spot on American Thanksgiving since the NHL adopted its wild-card format in 2013-14 have gone on to make the postseason. With the holiday a week away, the Penguins (7-12-2) and Blues (11-9-2) came into Thursday’s game in similar situations. Both teams entered the night outside the playoff picture with nearly identical recent form: the Penguins were 4-5-1 in their previous 10 games, while the Blues were 5-4-1. But only one of them looked like it had postseason aspirations. The Penguins’ new-look lines came out flying in the first period, playing with a speed that tilted the ice in their favor. They outshot the Blues 8-4, and Rickard Rakell accounted for five of those shots, including the one that put Pittsburgh up 1-0. As good as the Penguins were in the first, they were just as bad in the second. They gave up three goals and were outshot by an astounding 22-10 margin in the frame. item.title: Cocktail Thursday: South Carolina Edition
item.description: Are your Georgia Bulldogs getting ready to play a road game in the armpit of the southeast, against a team with absolutely nothing to lose? You’re probably nervous about that, and could probably use a drink. I can help you with that. i’m sure there’s a place on God‘s green earth I hate more than Williams –Brice Stadium in Columbia, South Carolina. But frankly at the moment I can’t call to mind what that place is. It’s an awful venue, filled with people I’d rather not have to engage with. It doesn’t help that many of my worst college football memories have taken place there. However, things are not quite as cocky in the land of Cocky as they have been for some past Bulldog visitsOne of the good things about playing the South Carolina Gamecocks in November rather than September is that they’ve generally given up on life at this point. The starch is out of their weird white hands towels, which they have essentially thrown in at this juncture. That being said, we must remain vigilant. A cornered South Carolina team is a dangerous South Carolina team. But this Gamecock squad is also a one-dimensional outfit. That one dimension is the multiple-dimensional talent talent of quarterback LaNorris Sellers. Sellers has accounted for 2100 of the Fightin’ Shane Beamers’ 2495 passing yards. He’a also the team’s leading rusher by a pretty wide margin (637 yards on the ground versus tailback Matt Fuller’s 530). Last week against Arkansas was the first time this season the Garnet and Black have been forced to run their offense through someone other than Sellers. And it went horribly. Backup Cutter Woods stepped in and stepped on every rake laid in front of him, tossing three interceptions in a 34-6 loss. Woods tossed 3 interceptions and the Gamecock rushing attack was borderline non-existent against a Razorback defense that isn’t in the same ball park as Glenn Schumann’s unit. After the game Beamer dissembled regarding the reason Sellers, who hadn’t even been listed on the availability report, didn’t play. I think there’a only one rational explanation. The South Carolina staff thought they could beat Arkansas without him and knew they couldn’t beat Georgia in his absence. That gamble may have placed Beamer back on the coaching hot seat with rivalry matchups against Georgia and Clemson still on the schedule. I can’t say Shane Beamer needs to beat Georgia to keep his job. But I can say confidently that without LaNorris Sellers he has no shot at beating Georgia. item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. item.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
item.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. item.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
item.description: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright “With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final . Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano . A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
